title: test(app-shell): stub useRecordPresence as the array the hook returns
body:
Fixes #8083

13 `RecordDetailView` test files stubbed `useRecordPresence` as
`{ viewers: [], others: [] }`. The hook returns `PresenceUser[]`
(`packages/collaboration/src/PresenceProvider.tsx`, anchor
`export function useRecordPresence`) and its only consumer reads
`recordPresence.length > 0` (`packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx`,
anchor `recordPresence.length`). An object has no `length`, so the presence row
was **structurally** unrenderable in those files. All 13 now stub `[]`, matching
the 9 files that already did.

Diff: 13 files, one line each, plus one changeset. Nothing else.

## Why "all 13 are still green" is not the evidence

Swapping `{ viewers: [], others: [] }` for `[]` leaves `recordPresence.length > 0`
`false` either way, so the row still does not render and the 13 stay green. **A
correct fix and a no-op produce byte-identical green.** The reading that
discriminates is *can it now go red* — feed the stub a non-empty array and the
row must render.

Measured with a mutation probe: the stub is filled with one `PresenceUser`, and
`PresenceAvatars` is replaced by a stand-in that **throws** `OS8083_PROBE_ROW_RENDERED`
on render. A file goes red exactly when the row reaches the DOM. Every leg
proves its edit landed on disk (injected-marker count, removed-marker count and
`git hash-object` before/after) before anything is run, and restores by
`git checkout HEAD -- path` verified with `git diff HEAD` empty. All runs went
through the shared heavy-verify lock; the verdict quoted is the runner's own
line, never a bare `$?`.

| leg | corpus | stub fed | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| probe validation (positive control) | the 9 already-correct files | `[user]` | **9/9 files red**, 46 cases, all `OS8083_PROBE_ROW_RENDERED` |
| before the fix | the 13 | `{ viewers: [user], others: [user] }` | **13/13 green, 99/99 cases, zero probe fires** |
| after the fix | the 13 | `[user]` | **12/13 files red**, 86 cases |
| the tree as shipped | all 22 | `[]` | 22 files, 157/157 green |

Row 2 is the card's thesis turned into a number: the object stub was fed users
in *both* of its fields and the row still could not render. Row 3 is the class
judgement — the branch is now pinnable.

**The 13th file, `RecordDetailView.expandFls-7230.test.tsx`, does not fire, and
that is a property of the file, not of the stub.** Its 6 cases resolve as soon as
a `findOne` is recorded, which happens while `RecordDetailView` is still in the
`isLoading` skeleton — an early return that sits above the presence chrome. Not
argued: with the same corrected stub and a one-shot case appended that awaits
the loaded tree, the presence element **is** found (7/7 green). So the stub is
capable there too; the file simply never observes the loaded tree.

## The second half — what broke when the row actually rendered

Nothing. **No assertion in any of the 13 was relying on the row being
unrenderable, and no existing assertion was touched.**

That negative was made in the strongest available form and then checked for
vacuity. The `PresenceAvatars` override line was **deleted** rather than
restubbed, so the real component came through the factory's
`...(await importOriginal())` and rendered its actual DOM, with the stub fed a
real `PresenceUser`. All 22 files: 157/157 green.

A green from a probe that renders nothing would be the very defect this card is
about, so the probe carries its own two-legged control on
`RecordDetailView.headerRefresh.test.tsx`:

- with the mutation, an appended case asserting the real component's
  `role="group"` stack is in the document **passes** (6/6);
- without the mutation, that same case **fails**:
  `AssertionError: real PresenceAvatars renders a role=group stack: expected 0 to be greater than 0`.

So the element counted is exclusively the real `PresenceAvatars`, and the 157/157
above is a measurement rather than an absence.

## Ablation

Prediction written before the run: from the committed tree, ablate exactly one
file (`headerRefresh`) back to the object stub, give the other 21 the array
stub, throwing stand-in everywhere; **20 of 22 red**, with `headerRefresh` green
(ablated) and `expandFls-7230` green (never reaches the loaded tree), and
nothing else moving.

Observed: `Test Files 20 failed | 2 passed (22)` / `Tests 128 failed | 29 passed (157)`.
The two green files are exactly `headerRefresh` and `expandFls-7230`. Restore
verified both ways: `git diff HEAD` empty over all 22 **and** the ablated file's
blob hash back to `c44714e63278`.

## 验收备注

**1. The two vi.mock gates cannot see this class — measured, not inferred, and
deliberately not extended here.**

- `check:vi-mock-specifiers` judges whether a **relative specifier resolves to a
  file**. These stubs mock the bare specifier `@object-ui/collaboration`, which
  the gate's own summary counts as `935 bare (out of scope)`.
- `check:vi-mock-inherit` judges whether a factory **obtains the real module**.
  All 13 already spread `...(await importOriginal())` and always did — they were
  compliant while carrying the drift. The gate judges the factory's inheritance,
  never an override's *value*.

Empirically: with all 13 object-shaped stubs put back on disk, both gates print
the same verdict line and the same exit code as on the repaired tree —
`✅ check-vi-mock-specifiers: OK` / `✅ check-vi-mock-inherit: OK`, exit 0 both.
**This class has no automated guard today; 13 drifted stubs were found only by a
hand census.** Extending a gate is a separate card and is not attempted here.

**2. Position axis, both carriers.**

- *(i) prose `file:line` citations.* `scripts/cross-file-line-citation-census.mjs`
  run three times — at the branch point, on this branch, and on the tree
  produced by a real `git merge --no-ff` of this branch into `origin/main` in a
  throwaway detached worktree. All three outputs are 634 lines and **byte-identical
  except the header's HEAD sha**. Zero citations moved.
- *(ii) machine-checked ledger keys that embed a line number, which the census
  cannot see.* The confirmed carrier `UNGATED_EXAMPLES` in
  `scripts/check-doc-example-types.mjs` holds 90 rows; **0 address app-shell or
  any `.test.tsx`**. Swept for the class, not just that instance: the only other
  literal `path:NUMBER` entries in the tree are `skills/objectui/guides/*`
  fixtures inside `scripts/__tests__/`, untouched. And there is no line-addressed
  citation into any of the 13 anywhere in the tree.
- The axis is safe for a structural reason as well: the diff replaces one line
  with one line in each file, and **every touched file kept its exact line
  count**, so nothing downstream of the edit shifted.

**3. `Clause-②: no`** — judged from the diff, not from convenience. 13
`*.test.tsx` lines plus one changeset: no new exported symbol, no new key on a
published payload, no schema key, closed-set member or registry entry. Measured
rather than asserted: every package's `files[]` ships `dist`, and no built `dist`
in the tree contains a single `*.test.*` artefact (positive control: the
published `useRecordPresence` symbol *is* present in `packages/collaboration/dist`).
Hence the empty-frontmatter changeset.

**4. `{ viewers, others }` exists nowhere in this repo as a real shape** — a
tree-wide sweep finds it only in the 13 stubs this PR removes, confirming the
card's reading that it was borrowed from a different presence surface.

## Verification

Run through `os-verify-lock.sh`, verdict lines quoted from the runner:

- the 22 affected files, before and after: `Test Files 22 passed (22)` / `Tests 157 passed (157)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the test files are covered): `VERDICT command-exit 0`. First attempt returned exit 2 with `Cannot find module '@object-ui/fields'` — a workspace not yet built, read as NOT MEASURED; re-run after `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/app-shell^...' build`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell run lint`: `✖ 2943 problems (0 errors, 2943 warnings)`, exit 0 — all warnings pre-existing, none on the touched lines.
- `pnpm check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `pnpm check:vi-mock-inherit`, `pnpm changeset:check`, `pnpm check:control-bytes`: all exit 0, verdict lines green.
- `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over all 14 paths: `NOT GOVERNED`.

**Declared narrowing.** Vitest's own config collects **669** test files for
`packages/app-shell/`; this branch ran **22** of them (count from vitest's own
`Test Files` line) plus the whole package's type-check and lint. The narrowing
excludes nothing that could move: a `vi.mock` factory is scoped to the file that
declares it, each of the 13 is an import leaf (nothing in the tree imports any of
them), and no touched file changed its line count. A 37-file presence-consumer
radius was queued for the lock twice and returned `exit 99` / `queue-timeout`
both times behind an 18-minute sibling holder — **NOT MEASURED**, not green and
not red. CI runs the full farm.
